subject: music
source_note: Topic structure follows the Eduqas/WJEC A-Level Music specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Appraising
units.blurb: Western Classical Tradition plus chosen areas of study

topics.name: Performance Recital
topics.blurb: Solo and/or ensemble performance demonstrating technical and expressive control

topics.name: Composition to a Brief
topics.blurb: Composing to a WJEC brief in the Western Classical Tradition

topics.name: Area-of-Study Composition
topics.blurb: A composition reflecting a chosen area of study

topics.name: AoS A: The Symphony
topics.blurb: Development of the symphony in the Western Classical Tradition (set works)

topics.name: AoS B/C/D: Rock & Pop / Musical Theatre / Jazz
topics.blurb: One chosen popular-idiom area of study

topics.name: AoS E/F: Into the 20th / 21st Century
topics.blurb: One chosen area exploring modern classical language (set works)

connections.why: The Western Classical Tradition supplies the harmonic and structural language for the brief
Twentieth/twenty-first century styles develop and react against the classical symphonic tradition
The chosen popular-idiom area of study models the second composition
Compositional craft from the brief transfers to the area-of-study composition
Area-of-study writing builds toward a fully independent free composition
Understanding symphonic style and structure informs expressive performance choices
Popular and jazz idioms are common contexts for the recital
Idiomatic knowledge of an instrument shapes idiomatic free composition
Modern compositional techniques expand the palette for free composition
Comparing classical and popular idioms sharpens stylistic listening across areas of study
